frozen_evidence_boundary: repository metadata and pinned git ref
pinned-source code search used only to locate bookmark/track deletion paths
no issue, PR, discussion, release-history, support or complaint evidence opened before Phase B/C freeze
raw_signal_observation: The Android bookmarks list routes track deletion through DeleteConfirmationDialogFragment before BookmarkManager.deleteTrack, while the per-bookmark delete action calls deleteBookmarkListItem and BookmarkManager.deleteBookmark directly without the same confirmation step.
material_claim: The source proves an asymmetry, but not that bookmarks and tracks share one confirmation contract. Whether bookmark deletion should gain a confirmation is an interaction-policy tradeoff involving deletion frequency, recoverability and friction, so sibling consistency alone does not authorize a build.
neta_next_move: Ask the product owner to state the deletion policy by object class and recovery path: which deletions require modal confirmation, which rely on undo/recovery, and why.
reversal_condition: If owner policy explicitly requires confirmation for bookmark deletion, permit the narrow confirmation change. If policy intentionally distinguishes frequent/recoverable bookmark deletion from higher-cost track/list deletion, preserve the asymmetry.
baseline_decision: BUILD: add the same confirmation dialog to bookmark deletion for consistency and protection against accidental destructive actions.

evidence: Issue #9859 frames deletion UX as a policy problem and explicitly proposes that deletion remain simple without confirmation dialogs in every app location while adding recovery.

In the #9859 discussion, repository member biodranik states that confirmation can become annoying for frequent deletion and distinguishes deletion/recovery policy by object and flow rather than requiring one universal guard.
Issue #5680 separately proposes confirmation for Favorite deletion, showing that the desired policy is genuinely contested/contextual rather than derivable from code symmetry alone.
adjudication.decision_delta: SURVIVED: the baseline would normalize the sibling paths immediately; adjudication shows that confirmation policy is explicitly product-owned and context-dependent, so Neta correctly prevented an unjustified consistency build.
adjudication.lesson: A destructive-action asymmetry can be intentional when frequency, recoverability and consequence differ. Similar delete verbs do not establish a shared confirmation contract.
